Pre-Ride Safety Check: POWDDERS

The POWDDERS acronym covers everything you need to check before every ride. Takes 2 minutes and could save your life. Read our Best Motorcycle Roads in Scotland: 15 Must-Ride Routes guide for more. Read our Motorcycle Helmet Safety Ratings Explained guide for more. Read our Wales: 5 Must-Ride Motorcycle Roads guide for more. Read our Motorcycle Hand Signals Every Rider Should Know guide for more. Read our What to Do After a Motorcycle Accident guide for more. Read our Be Seen: Visibility Tips for UK Motorcyclists guide for more.

  • P — Petrol: Check fuel level, plan fuel stops.
  • O — Oil: Check level through sight glass or dipstick.
  • W — Water: Check coolant level (if liquid-cooled).
  • D — Damage: Walk around, check for leaks, loose parts, cracks.
  • D — Drive Chain: Check tension (20–30mm slack), lubrication, sprocket wear.
  • E — Electrics: Test lights, indicators, brake lights, horn.
  • R — Rubber (Tyres): Check pressure, tread depth (min 1mm legal, 2mm+ recommended), sidewall damage.
  • S — Steering: Check steering head bearing play, smooth turning.
keyTakeaways: POWDDERS is a memorable acronym covering eight pre-ride safety checks.
The check takes about two minutes and can prevent a breakdown or crash.
Drive chain slack should be around 20 to 30mm, with proper lubrication.
Tyres need correct pressure and at least the 1mm legal minimum tread, ideally 2mm-plus.
The checks cover petrol, oil, water, damage, chain, electrics, rubber and steering.

faq.a: POWDDERS is a pre-ride checklist standing for Petrol, Oil, Water, Damage, Drive chain, Electrics, Rubber (tyres) and Steering. Running through it before every ride takes about two minutes and catches problems like low fluids, a slack chain, blown bulbs or under-inflated tyres before they cause a breakdown or accident.

faq.q: How much chain slack should a motorcycle have?
faq.a: Most bikes need around 20 to 30mm of slack in the drive chain, but always check your owner's manual for the exact figure, as it varies by model. Too tight and the chain can bind or snap; too loose and it can jump the sprockets. Also check the chain is properly lubricated and the sprocket teeth are not hooked.

faq.q: What is the legal tyre tread depth in the UK?
faq.a: The UK legal minimum for motorcycle tyres is 1mm of tread depth across three-quarters of the breadth of the tread. For safety, most riders replace tyres at around 2mm or more, as grip in the wet drops off significantly before the legal limit. Check pressures and look for sidewall damage during the R (rubber) check.

faq.q: How long does a pre-ride check take?
faq.a: A full POWDDERS check takes only about two minutes once you are familiar with it, yet it can prevent serious problems. Making it a habit before every ride means faults like a failed brake light, low oil or a soft tyre are spotted in the driveway rather than discovered dangerously out on the road.

faq.q: Do I need to check coolant on every bike?
faq.a: The W (water) check applies to liquid-cooled bikes, where you should confirm the coolant is at the correct level in the expansion tank. Air-cooled bikes have no coolant to check, so you can skip that step. Either way, look for any signs of leaking fluid during the damage check, as it can signal a developing fault.
